steps.summary: exceptions with k^2 <= n < k^3 have bounded k (from Konyagin's lower bound on g(k), which exceeds k^3 for large k)
exceptions with n >= k^3 have bounded k (the open part: Ecklund's conjecture where n/k >= k^2)
Baker-Harman-Pintz, as on erdos-1094--h2--h2 (the same statement, erdos-1094--h2--h2--h1)
BHP fails, or van Doorn-Tang Theorem 1.1 holds, as on erdos-1094--h2--h2 (the same statement, erdos-1094--h2--h2--h2)
for large k no exception has k^2 <= n < k(k + 3k^(21/40)), given k*(n/k) divides k!; follows from g(k) > k^2 + 3k^(61/40)
Baker-Harman-Pintz: for large k, (k, k + k^(21/40)) holds at least C k^(21/40) / log k primes; exactly van Doorn and Tang's axiom bhp
BHP fails, or van Doorn-Tang Theorem 1.1 holds (for large k and 2k < n <= exp(log^2 k/(20 log log k)) a prime in (k, k+3k^(21/40)) divides (n-k)...(n-1)); their Lean file proves this
the open core that remains: for large k no exception has n >= k^3 and n+1 > exp(log^2 k/(20 log log k)), given k*(n/k) divides k!
vdT case_small: 2k < n <= k^(2-θ)/2, as ¬BHP ∨ case
vdT case_medium: k^(2-θ)/2 < n <= k²/log²k, as ¬BHP ∨ case
vdT case_mediumlarge: k²/log²k < n <= k^(2+θ)/2, as ¬BHP ∨ case
vdT case_large (Konyagin step): k^(2+θ)/2 < n <= exp(log²k/(20 log log k)), as ¬BHP ∨ case
[ELS] 1993, cited by GR §5e p.24: minFac C(n,k) > k, 2k <= n, k large imply k^2 <= C * n * log2 k.
GR §5e pp.24-25 via (5.1) (Sander): for every C, for k large, k^2 <= C n log2 k, n < k^2, some prime p in (k/2, 11k/20) has n mod p < k mod p.
For all large even k and every 2k <= n < k^2, some prime p <= k has n mod p < k mod p.
For all large odd k and every odd n with 2k <= n < k^2, some prime p <= k has n mod p < k mod p.
Used by GR p.25 ("≫ k"): for large k, the sum of log p over primes k/2 < p < 11k/20 is at least k/100 (PNT on (x, 1.1x)).
GR (5.1), p.18, from Sander [Sa2] via Lemma 5.1: for every C, eps > 0 and large k with k^2 <= C n log2 k, n < k^2: |sum over those p of ({n/p} - 1/2) log p| <= eps k.
